question: Does a make-probability model that reads the NBA shot type (ACTION_TYPE) and pre-shot game context, as well as location, predict whether a field-goal attempt goes in better than league make rates by zone and distance, on whole seasons it never saw? And, using the accepted model (or the baseline if none is accepted), how many points per 100 shots does each player score above or below the expected value of their shots?
inputs: Shots: every regular-season NBA ShotChartDetail row with SHOT_ATTEMPTED_FLAG = 1, 2014-15 to 2025-26, from the retained shufinskiy/nba_data archives at pinned revision e829d4678be1e075f99e5d41a1c5f97089be446b (the same bytes R03 read for rim FG%), each archive checked against its SHA-256 before reading: shotdetail 2014 e2bf7530..., 2015 ac48fad6..., 2016 0681285a..., 2017 a62d25aa..., 2018 c6588909..., 2019 0c6002cb..., 2020 02916ac0..., 2021 5b56b683..., 2022 62533f4e..., 2023 303e71f9..., 2024 950100f9..., 2025 dcb6c29e.... Fields read: GAME_ID, GAME_EVENT_ID, PLAYER_ID, TEAM_ID, GAME_DATE, PERIOD, MINUTES_REMAINING, SECONDS_REMAINING, ACTION_TYPE, SHOT_TYPE, SHOT_ZONE_BASIC, SHOT_ZONE_AREA, SHOT_ZONE_RANGE, SHOT_DISTANCE, LOC_X, LOC_Y, SHOT_MADE_FLAG.

Play-by-play: NBA PlayByPlayV3 (nbastatsv3) regular-season archives from the same revision, pinned by the R01 observations (history-observations/31544bdf for 2014 to 2022, observations/068decb9 for 2023 to 2025) and checked against their SHA-256: 2014 76a53982..., 2015 7bbb1e8a..., 2016 6c94890f..., 2017 e9fedc33..., 2018 a8c05607..., 2019 3fc651e4..., 2020 8bbd2406..., 2021 f44ec8a4..., 2022 42c24abf..., 2023 3a697621..., 2024 38fb8bfb..., 2025 790a01ea....

Shot tables: built before this registration by courtlens.evaluation.expected_shot_v2_data (two builds, identical content hashes) and pinned here; the runner refuses a table whose content SHA-256 differs: 2014-15 7ccd1619e781489f5c1eb9bcff56b78f3eb86d34ba09a44bda3df4d58a8ddfb9, 2015-16 44f482010dabf01975213685d17f102670cbb5d12843b905adcabd8a1f04bcac, 2016-17 0a4b15879f67b81b4610409e380729b979b21a881d0f2e1146be4fa5c32f0938, 2017-18 a2a598e77cbbed4c3e2a2c78fefa2b2fa68304cd4f8f6825654d5cd9b628014a, 2018-19 4b1126e4a5edb81af1f952813768c6c3970158d7f5bad3a2997f6c64fd7690e0, 2019-20 a5b473aeb2529da4d1e858cba29ad4d394a15e58377c7832dbf27aed54c50fa2, 2020-21 924da9a149eb0d39d731e9af3b07036fd828b273ce46c29eadc268bdc62aed3d, 2021-22 92975a791d161f5e7ac77768ea2badc98b12e7ac2c5442d621df73ca6cce886a, 2022-23 84a66b41afa88d7e5d5c1c4d7a34bc6ce4bbc7a4117781aabec0cbfbe2ceb0e4, 2023-24 196833fff2088c9bb8adf3b0b941eab76cb3e9ee2f8d848adca8f4ecc1391148, 2024-25 e529ebe0b5c795c8b7c8433b0bba2b1c0600994027c29e11a52db61581b65caf, 2025-26 5c68c0614ad40a26ede07e5fe54d586ffe3da013c26545c71f72811061b9b150.

DATA CHECK (done before this registration; it read counts, join results and the action-type vocabulary by split role, and one outcome cross-tab used only to exclude a feature, never a make rate by feature). Rows (FGA) and games per season: 2014-15 205,550 / 1,230; 2015-16 207,893 / 1,230; 2016-17 209,929 / 1,230; 2017-18 211,707 / 1,230; 2018-19 219,458 / 1,230; 2019-20 188,116 / 1,059; 2020-21 190,983 / 1,080; 2021-22 216,722 / 1,230; 2022-23 217,218 / 1,230; 2023-24 218,701 / 1,230; 2024-25 219,527 / 1,230; 2025-26 219,160 / 1,230. Every shot-chart game has play-by-play. Join by (GAME_ID, GAME_EVENT_ID = actionNumber), requiring the same player, result and period: 100% of shots in 2014-15, 2015-16, 2018-19, 2019-20, 2020-21, 2021-22; 2016-17 99.9995% (1 player differs); 2017-18 99.9235% (122 no event, 35 player differs, 5 result differs); 2022-23 99.9991% (2); 2023-24 99.9995% (1); 2024-25 99.9995% (1); 2025-26 99.9982% (4). Possession context known for 99.56% (2017-18) to 99.72% (2014-15, 2015-16) of shots; the rest are unknown after a mid-period jump ball or an unparseable clock (535 to 673 per season), a possession conflict (16 to 209 per season, mostly free throws after away-from-play fouls, where the shooting team keeps the ball), or no join.

Counts differ from the sealed B26 admission by at most two rows per season (2023-24: 218,701 here, 218,700 eligible there), because B26 applied six reviewed corrections to 2023-24 to 2025-26. v2 reads the archive rows as they are and does not reuse the sealed B26 dataset or its tables.
method: TARGET. y = SHOT_MADE_FLAG (1 made, 0 missed) for every field-goal attempt. Shot value v = 3 if SHOT_TYPE is '3PT Field Goal', else 2 (known before the shot from its location). Expected points of a shot = v * p, with p the make probability; actual points = v * y. FREE THROWS ARE EXCLUDED: a fouled missed shot is not a field-goal attempt and never appears in the shot chart, so adding and-one free throws (4,851 to 6,560 per season, detected as the shooter's free throw 1 of 1 at the same clock) would credit only fouled shots that went in. Expected points therefore cover field-goal points only; shooting-foul value is R06's free-throw component.

FEATURES. All describe the moment before the shot; NONE may read the shot's result or anything after it. From the shot chart: LOC_X, LOC_Y (tenths of feet), SHOT_DISTANCE (feet), shot value, SHOT_ZONE_BASIC, SHOT_ZONE_AREA, ACTION_TYPE (the NBA's shot-type coding: driving, pull-up, step-back, floating, dunk, putback, alley-oop and so on), PERIOD, seconds left in the period (MINUTES_REMAINING, SECONDS_REMAINING). From the play-by-play replay (domain.expected_shot_v2.game_context): score margin before the shot (shooting team minus opponent; the shot's own points are not yet added), seconds since the shooting team gained possession (the transition proxy), whether the possession includes an own offensive rebound before the shot, and seconds since that rebound. Possession gains: period start (open until the first action), opponent made field goal, opponent made last regular free throw, own defensive rebound of an opponent's missed shot or missed last free throw, opponent turnover; team rebounds and team turnovers count (their team id sits in personId). An own offensive rebound keeps the possession and its start (after a missed and-one free throw, the possession starts at the rebound). A mid-period jump ball makes the possession unknown until the next gain. Technical, flagrant and clear-path free throws change nothing. A shot by a team the replay does not hold possession for is unknown, never guessed.

EXCLUDED FEATURES. Assisted / unassisted: the play-by-play records an assist only on made shots (data check: 0 of 1,355,809 missed shots in 2014-15 to 2025-26 carry an assist; 65,610 of 103,739 makes in 2023-24 do), so it reveals the outcome and is not a pre-shot feature. Shooter identity: player shot-making is measured against the model, so the model never sees who shoots. Closest defender, touch time, dribbles and shot clock: not in free data. Season or date: no time trend; drift is handled by calibration.

UNKNOWN VALUES. A shot without a join keeps its shot-chart features; its context is unknown. Unknown possession values are NaN for LightGBM (native missing-value handling) and, for the logistic model, a zero row in the possession block plus a 'possession unknown' indicator. Unknown is never imputed as zero seconds or as no offensive rebound. No shot is dropped.

VOCABULARIES (training seasons only). ACTION_TYPE values with at least 500 training attempts keep their own category; the rest, and any value first seen after training, map to 'other'. The same rule applies to the SHOT_ZONE_BASIC x SHOT_ZONE_AREA cell. Data check: 15 action types appear only in training seasons (for example 'Tip Shot', 'Driving Bank shot'); generic 'Layup Shot' falls from about 13,600 a season in training to about 3,300 in test, a coding change rather than a play change. Calibration on 2023-24 is the registered response to this drift.

BASELINE (league zone and distance rates). p = (makes + 1) / (attempts + 2) of training shots in the cell (SHOT_ZONE_BASIC, distance in whole feet clipped to 0..40, with 41+ as one band). A cell with fewer than 100 training attempts falls back to its SHOT_ZONE_BASIC rate, smoothed the same way. Location only, like v1's zone x 2/3 baseline.

REFERENCE (descriptive, no gate): the same smoothed table by (SHOT_ZONE_BASIC, ACTION_TYPE category), falling back to the zone rate under 100 attempts. It shows how much of any gain comes from the shot type alone.

CANDIDATE 1: logistic regression. Design: cubic B-spline basis of distance clipped to [0, 50] with fixed knots [0, 1, 3, 5, 8, 12, 16, 20, 22, 24, 26, 30, 40, 50] (sklearn SplineTransformer, degree 3, extrapolation 'constant'); 3-point indicator; one-hot ACTION_TYPE category; one-hot zone cell; one-hot period (1, 2, 3, 4, overtime); one-hot seconds left in the period (<= 2, (2, 5], (5, 24], > 24); margin clipped to [-30, 30] and its absolute value, both divided by 10; B-spline basis of possession seconds clipped to [0, 60] with knots [0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 14, 18, 22, 26, 35, 60], zeroed when unknown; possession-unknown indicator; offensive-rebound indicator; one-hot seconds since the offensive rebound (<= 2, (2, 6], > 6) when there was one. LogisticRegression(C=1.0, solver='lbfgs', max_iter=3000, tol=1e-6), intercept unpenalized by sklearn default, sparse design, no class weights.

CANDIDATES 2 and 3: LightGBM 4.7.0 binary classifiers, features loc_x, loc_y, distance, value, action-type category and zone cell (as categorical features), period, seconds left, margin, possession seconds, offensive-rebound indicator (-1 unknown -> NaN), seconds since the rebound. Fixed settings: learning_rate 0.05, n_estimators 600, min_child_samples 200, reg_lambda 1.0, feature_fraction 1.0, no bagging, max_bin 255, deterministic true, force_row_wise true, num_threads 1, seed 5005. The fixed grid is num_leaves in {31 (candidate 2), 127 (candidate 3)}. No early stopping: no season is used to choose the number of trees.

CONVERGENCE AND CHECKS (fail loudly). The logistic fit must finish with n_iter_ < max_iter and no ConvergenceWarning (warnings are raised as errors). Each LightGBM model must contain exactly 600 trees, and its training log loss after the last tree must be below that after the first. Every Platt calibration must converge (scipy L-BFGS-B success). Every prediction and metric must be finite; probabilities are clipped to [1e-6, 1 - 1e-6] only inside log loss. The runner checks each constant it uses against this registration's parameters and refuses to start on a mismatch.

CHRONOLOGICAL SPLIT. Train: 2014-15 to 2021-22 (1,650,358 shots). Select: 2022-23 (217,218). Calibrate: 2023-24 (218,701). Final test: 2024-25 and 2025-26 (438,687). Whole seasons; no game is split. Models are fitted once on the training seasons and never refitted on later seasons.

SELECTION (2022-23 only, uncalibrated). Every candidate and the baseline predict 2022-23. The candidate with the lowest Brier score is chosen (ties: earlier candidate). SELECTION GATE, identical to v1's: the chosen candidate's relative Brier improvement over the baseline, 1 - Brier(candidate) / Brier(baseline), must be at least 1%. If it is not, no candidate is accepted, the baseline is used for player shot-making, and the result is a second negative result.

CALIBRATION (2023-24 only). Platt scaling: p' = sigmoid(a + b * logit(p)), fitted by unpenalized maximum likelihood (scipy L-BFGS-B) on 2023-24, separately for the chosen candidate (if the gate passed), the baseline and the reference. Fitted once; never refitted on test seasons.

RUN ORDER. A choice pass (--choice-only) fits everything, scores 2022-23, writes the choice file and stops; it is read before the test pass. The test pass loads the saved models (checked by SHA-256), calibrates on 2023-24 and scores 2024-25 and 2025-26. Any change after the choice pass is read, or any change at all after the test is read (including serving-only changes), is disclosed; analysis changes require courtlens-expected-shot-v3.

PLAYER SHOT-MAKING (descriptive). For each player-season in 2022-23 to 2025-26 (the seasons no model was trained on), with p from the calibrated accepted candidate, or the calibrated baseline if none is accepted: n = FGA; PPS = sum(v * y) / n; xPPS = sum(v * p') / n (expected points per shot, the shot-quality value); league term L = (sum(v * y) - sum(v * p')) / N over every shot of that season; SHOT-MAKING = 100 * ((PPS - xPPS) - L), points per 100 shots against the expected value of the same shots, relative to the league in the same season. Players' shots on every team are pooled; the primary team is the one with the most shots. Seasons 2014-15 to 2021-22 are training seasons and are not served for players (reason 'training_season').

CREDIT. ShotQuality and the oSQ / oMake decomposition are ShotQuality's and Databallr's concepts (databallr.com ShotQuality RAPM page); CourtLens does not use the paid ShotQuality feed and its numbers are its own. Shot and play-by-play data: NBA Stats via shufinskiy/nba_data.
selection: The only choice made from outcomes is the candidate with the lowest 2022-23 Brier score, followed by the 1% selection gate. Features, knots, bands, vocabularies, the LightGBM grid and every threshold are fixed here. Test seasons (2024-25, 2025-26) are never used for any choice. Disclosure: the earlier v1 attempt read selection-half metrics of a location-only model on part of 2024-25, and 2025-26 had been inspected before v1 (see docs/research/b26-expected-shot-result.md). No v2 choice reads either season, but they are not unseen data in the strictest sense.
uncertainty: Game-cluster bootstrap: 2,000 replicates, seed 5005, numpy default_rng, whole games resampled with replacement within the scored seasons (multinomial game counts). Each replicate recomputes Brier, log loss and expected-point MAE for every model on the same resample, and their differences and relative improvements. 95% percentile intervals. Per-season and per-slice intervals use the same procedure within that subset and are unadjusted for multiple comparisons. Player shot-making intervals: 2,000-replicate bootstrap of the player's own games (seed 5005 + season index, players in sorted id order), 95% percentile interval of 100 * ((PPS - xPPS) - L) with L and the model fixed; they show shot-outcome noise given the model, not model uncertainty. Shot-making is served only with at least 300 FGA in the season; fewer is unknown with reason 'small_sample'.
evaluation: Selection season 2022-23, uncalibrated: Brier, log loss, expected-point MAE and ECE for the baseline, the reference and each candidate, with intervals for differences from the baseline; the chosen candidate and the gate outcome.
Test seasons, calibrated (and uncalibrated, reported): the same metrics pooled and per season for the baseline, the reference and the accepted candidate; differences from the baseline with intervals.
Calibration curves on the pooled test seasons: 20 equal-count bins (count, mean predicted, observed rate) for the baseline and the accepted candidate; ECE over 10 equal-width bins.

Slices on the pooled test seasons (reported, no gate; at least 200 attempts): SHOT_ZONE_BASIC, shot value, test season, possession seconds (<= 6, (6, 14], > 14, unknown), offensive-rebound possession.
Player shot-making for 2022-23 to 2025-26 with intervals and every unknown with its reason; the league term L per season.

Descriptive persistence (no gate): weighted correlation (weight = harmonic mean of FGA) of player shot-making in consecutive served seasons (2022-23 to 2023-24, 2023-24 to 2024-25, 2024-25 to 2025-26), pooled, for players with at least 300 FGA in both, and the same for xPPS and for PPS minus the league PPS, with player-cluster bootstrap intervals (2,000 replicates, seed 5005).
Reproducibility: two runs from the seed give the same results hash.
acceptance: Selection: the chosen candidate improves 2022-23 Brier by at least 1% relative to the baseline (point estimate). Otherwise stop: no candidate is accepted.

Test (pooled 2024-25 and 2025-26, calibrated), all three for acceptance: (1) relative Brier improvement of at least 1% and the 95% interval of Brier(baseline) - Brier(candidate) above 0; (2) the 95% interval of LogLoss(baseline) - LogLoss(candidate) above 0; (3) candidate ECE (10 equal-width bins) at most 0.02. Each failed gate is named. If any fails, the candidate is not accepted and player shot-making uses the calibrated baseline.
Every fit and calibration converged, and every served number is finite.
Every shot has a join status and every unknown context value a named reason; every player-season served for 2022-23 to 2025-26 has a status.
Two runs give the same results hash.
The result is published whichever way it goes, including a second negative result.
outputs: data/derived/expected-shot-v2/runs/<run>/ (choice file, saved models with SHA-256, predictions summary)
docs/evidence/research/r05/results.json (registration receipt, data check, selection, test, calibration and persistence sections of the frozen file)
limitations: No defender, shot-clock, dribble or touch data: the model knows where and how a shot was taken and the game situation, not how well it was contested. ShotQuality's paid model uses tracking data; this does not.
ACTION_TYPE is the NBA scorer's label; its coding changed over the seasons (for example generic 'Layup Shot' became rarer), which calibration on 2023-24 only partly absorbs.
Field-goal points only: free throws and fouled shots are not modelled.
Possession seconds come from the play-by-play clock (whole seconds before about 2019-20) and possession rules above; 0.28% to 0.44% of shots per season are unknown.
Shot-making intervals cover shot-outcome noise for a fixed model; they do not include model error or the league term's uncertainty.
Shot-making is measured against a model that does not know the shooter, so a player's shot-making mixes skill with whatever the model cannot see (defenders, shot clock).
negative_result_policy: Publish every number whatever it shows, including a failed selection gate (a second negative result), a failed test gate, and player shot-making from the baseline.
